title: The Lantern in the Crystal Cave

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Place a real candle on a stable surface at a comfortable distance, away from anything flammable. Sit upright without becoming rigid.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If you have an eye condition, recent eye surgery, migraine sensitivity, or discomfort, skip the flame and use a gentle non-bright point instead.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [faint cave air sounds] Let the gaze rest near the brightest part of the flame. Imagine it standing inside a quiet crystal cave.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Keep the eyes soft. Reflections may shimmer, but the central lantern remains your simple place of return.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Blink whenever needed. This is attention training, not a contest with your eyelids.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the flame's colour, shape, and tiny movements while the body stays broad and relaxed around seeing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] When thought carries you down another tunnel, acknowledge it and come back to the lantern.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the breath move naturally. The flame does not need your breathing to remain alive.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Close the eyes now and notice any after-image floating behind the lids.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest attention on the inner light while it changes colour, moves, fades, or disappears completely.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Open the eyes and return to the real flame. Let the outer lantern become clear again.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Stay for another gentle interval, blinking freely and relaxing the muscles around the eyes.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice that steadiness does not mean stillness. The flame dances while attention learns to remain.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Close the eyes once more. Receive the after-image without trying to pin it in place.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release even the inner image. Rest in the dark cave of awareness for a few quiet breaths.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Open your eyes, look away from the flame, and let ordinary shapes and colours return.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Extinguish the candle safely. Carry the practice as a calm return, never as strain.
